summary.headline: JM Financial Q2 FY27 net revenue hit INR712 crores and PAT INR240 crores, with corporate advisory and capital markets PAT up 4x QoQ to INR127 crores.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was driven by a sharp rebound in corporate advisory and capital markets after a weak April-May, with segment net revenue up 2.5x QoQ to INR286 crores. Consolidated net revenue was INR712 crores and PAT after minority interest INR240 crores; half-year net revenue rose 7% to about INR1,600 crores and PAT to INR531 crores. Private markets disbursements doubled to INR977 crores, drawing cash down from INR3,077 crores to INR1,691 crores, and management said it will resume borrowing to fund growth. Wealth recurring AUM including loans reached about INR40,000 crores (+17% YoY), while the wealth business only broke even in September.

segments.name: Corporate advisory and capital markets
segments.commentary: Q2 net revenue INR286 crores (2.5x QoQ), PAT INR127 crores (4x QoQ), annualised ROE about 36%. Ranked #1 in IPOs and QIPs with INR83,000 crores of closed transactions in Q2; INR130,000 crores filed with regulator for execution over the next 12 months. Deal sizes cut by about INR10,000 crores, costing an estimated 40-50 bps (INR40-50 crores) of fees.

segments.name: Private markets
segments.commentary: Disbursements doubled to INR977 crores in Q2, mainly bespoke; standard loans up 22% YoY to INR4,748 crores. Cash fell from INR3,077 crores to INR1,691 crores; debt-equity 0.8x against a 4x limit. Q2 net revenue INR120 crores, PAT after NCI INR77 crores.

segments.name: Wealth management
segments.commentary: Recurring AUM INR37,000 crores (+16% YoY), recurring AUM including loans about INR40,000 crores (+17%); wealth loan book up 30% YoY to about INR2,600 crores. Sales and RM strength 948 professionals across 71 branches; RM count reduced on productivity. Gross recurring yield about 51 bps and net about 35 bps.

segments.name: Asset management
segments.commentary: First close of maiden Pre-IPO Fund at over INR700 crores; AIF AUM including commitments INR1,063 crores. Average non-liquid AUM about INR11,200 crores (+7% QoQ). MF management fees Q2 INR12 crores (+24%); AMC losses after minority INR10 crores in Q2.

segments.name: Affordable home loans
segments.commentary: AUM about INR3,900 crores (+30% YoY), disbursements +48% YoY, 152 branches and about 37,500 customers. Half-year revenue INR256 crores (+22%) and half-year PAT INR35 crores (+28%).

guidance_outlook: Corporate advisory and capital markets: 15-20% growth over the next 3-5 years; about 15% assumed for the rest of FY27.
Private markets: around 20% loan book growth and around 15% investment book growth; will resume borrowing from next quarter as cash runs to a floor of about INR1,000 crores.

Wealth management: 20-25% AUM growth, subject to market; management expects double-digit recurring AUM growth and full-year profitability in FY28, about three to four quarters later than originally planned.
Asset management: 15-20% growth; SIF platform planned early next year; second performing credit fund first close targeted this financial year.
Group: about 20% blended growth for at least five years; revenue growth of 15-20% should translate into 20-25% profit growth; target mid-teens ROE toward the end of the investment cycle.
Write-backs on impairments: about INR250 crores targeted in FY27, with only INR15 crores achieved in H1; final dividend to be decided on the next two quarters' results.
capex_capacity: Private markets: cash fell to INR1,691 crores; management wants to hold at least INR1,000 crores and will borrow from Q3 FY27 onward.
ARC: after a large account resolved in October (INR330-340 crores liquidity), about INR2,000 crores of SR investments remain, to be realised over 18-24 months at modelled returns of 16-18%.
Wealth: recruitment phase to continue, with a focus on productivity in the next six months; recruiting again from FY28 onward (build-out through 2030).
AMC: building alternatives and SIF platforms; GIFT City and Singapore VCC offerings, with more than USD225 million AUM and USD30-40 million quarterly net additions.
Holding company liquidity: NSE shares listed recently under a six-month lockup expiring March 2027.
demand_pricing: Markets were choppy; primary-market revival from June, with July-September strong and October described as decent; FPI participation returned to primary markets.
Deal sizes were cut, costing an estimated INR40-50 crores of fee revenue in the quarter.
Real estate lending pricing is a constraint: management requires 200-300 bps above corporate, and says there is no stress in its metros.
Broking industry revenue fell in H1 due to regulatory changes; JM says it is holding and gaining cash market share.
Recurring revenue is about 50% of total; brokerage adds 12-15%, so about 62-65% is recurring-type income, with the rest transactional.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the investment banking pipeline depends on market conditions, and is it M&A or market-independent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said June revived primary markets; a large part of the pipeline has traded up post listing. Pipeline is robust, and management expects to complete much of it in the next five months if momentum holds.

qa_highlights.question: Will private credit loan growth continue, and what drives the lower yield on cash and investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said lending is disciplined and lumpy; it will borrow from next quarter and expects 20% loan growth. Yield dip is attributed to lower real estate lending (priced 200-300 bps above corporate) and the investment book being largely cash.

qa_highlights.question: Why does net revenue in private markets not grow YoY despite higher loan yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to fair value marks, higher cash in the prior year, and recovery-led interest in H1 FY26. Half-year net revenue is up 63% (INR582 crores), and it expects further write-backs of about INR250 crores this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is wealth growth slower, and what is the RM productivity outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: RM reduction was planned for productivity, with recruitment resuming by FY-end. Broking revenue was flat due to regulation; existing RMs add about INR75 crores net new money each, new cohort about half. Recurring AUM is expected to grow in double digits.

qa_highlights.question: Why do private markets and corporate advisory not peak together, and why not demerge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ARC is largely uncorrelated to capital markets and the bespoke book is linked to it. Demerger has been considered, but synergies with wealth and AMC are high and the company wants to scale first.

qa_highlights.question: Why no large share buyback at a deep discount to NAV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said much of the liquidity sits in NBFCs, and extracting it requires a holding-company tax hit. The NSE stake lockup ends March 2027, and capital allocation will be decided in April-May 2027. Promoters increased their stake by about 1% last quarter.

risks_watch: Capital markets revenue depends on market conditions; deal sizes were cut in the quarter and transactional income is volatile.
ARC and NPA recoveries are lumpy; INR250 crores of write-backs targeted for FY27 with only INR15 crores so far.
Wealth profitability is delayed to FY28; RM productivity and net new money per cohort need to improve.
Private credit yields are under pressure, with real estate priced at a discount to management's required spread; borrowing restart will test margins.
Equity and alternative mark-to-market volatility (e.g., Gokaldas Exports after US tariffs) can swing reported PAT.
Capital allocation: large liquidity in NBFCs and the NSE stake lockup (until March 2027) gate a potential buyback.
summary.management_tone: Confident on capital markets, pipeline and the private markets recovery, with a clear focus on execution. Cautious and somewhat evasive on wealth profitability timing, ARC recovery timing, and buyback or capital return, deferring those decisions to April-May 2027.
key_quotes: We still have INR130,000 crores worth of transactions, which are already filed with the regulator for execution over the next 12 months, and many more to be filed this quarter and next quarter.
I can confidently say that we have bottomed.
As a promoter family, we creeped 1% last quarter.
